The key to this mechanism is understanding that my ranking only affects which school I get *within* my "Obtainable Schools" set. It doesn't change what's in that set. Since I want to get the best school possible, I should rank the schools in my true preference order. This ensures that if my "Obtainable Schools" set contains, for example, x, y, and w, I'll get x (my most preferred). If it contains only y and w, I'll get y, and so on. There's no strategic reason to misrepresent my preferences because doing so could only lead to getting a *worse* school from within my Obtainable Schools.

My true preference order is x > z > y > w.
